aiOverview.content: Good Friday services do not include a traditional Mass or the consecration of the Eucharist, but rather a solemn "Liturgy of the Lord's Passion" typically held around 3 p.m.. The service focuses on the crucifixion, featuring the Liturgy of the Word, the Adoration of the Holy Cross, and Holy Communion using bread consecrated on Holy Thursday. Key Elements of the Good Friday Liturgy No Mass: It is the only day of the year Catholics do not celebrate the Eucharist. Structure: The service consists of three parts: the Liturgy of the Word, the Veneration of the Cross, and Holy Communion. Solemn Atmosphere: The altar is left completely bare, and the service often begins in silence without an entrance procession. Adoration of the Cross: A central act where the cross is brought to the altar and honored by the faithful. Prostration: The priest prostrates himself in silent prayer at the beginning of the service. Veneration: The service usually features the Veneration of the Cross, often starting at 3 p.m., the traditional hour of Jesus' death. Communion: Communion is received from hosts consecrated at the Mass of the Lord's Supper on Holy Thursday. Devotions and Traditions Fasting & Abstinence: Good Friday is a mandatory day of fasting and abstinence from meat in the Catholic Church. Stations of the Cross: Many parishes hold the Stations of the Cross, often in the form of a public procession. Liturgical Color: Red is worn to symbolize the passion and blood of Christ. Silent Prayer: The day is marked by prayerful reflection, often including the "Three Hours' Devotion".
